title: Pure Component Render Inspector
subtopicTitle: Render Phase vs Commit Phase Mechanics
concept: Idempotence and Purity in Component Body
problemStatement: Implement `verifyRenderPurity(componentFn, props)` that runs `componentFn(props)` twice consecutively. If the output varies or side-effect counters change between runs, returns `{ isPure: false }`, otherwise `{ isPure: true, output }`.
interviewTrap: React StrictMode renders components TWICE in development specifically to uncover impure renders and accidental side effects.

testCases.name: Identifies pure deterministic render
testCases.testFn: const PureComp = p => ({ tag: 'h1', text: p.name }); return verifyRenderPurity(PureComp, { name: 'Alice' }).isPure;

testCases.name: Flags impure component mutating external counter
testCases.testFn: let globalCount = 0; const ImpureComp = () => ({ val: ++globalCount }); return verifyRenderPurity(ImpureComp, {}).isPure;

details.name: Flags impure component mutating external counter

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React's pipeline is divided into two distinct phases: The **Render Phase** (pure computation, diffing, finding changes) and the **Commit Phase** (applying changes to the host DOM and executing side-effects). A Pure Component Render Inspector checks whether component functions remain pure and side-effect free during the render phase.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Accept a component render function and props.
Instrument global environment to intercept side-effects (e.g. DOM mutations, global variable writes).
Invoke the component render function twice (simulating React's `<StrictMode>` double-render in development).
Compare the two outputs: both renders must return identical element trees without mutating external state.
Report any detected impurities or differences.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Concurrent Mode, the Render Phase can be paused, aborted, restarted, or thrown away if higher-priority work arrives. If a component performs side-effects (e.g. `window.count++`) during render, those side-effects execute unpredictably multiple times.

complexity.time: O(R) where R is the render execution time of the component.

edgeCasesHandled: Pure functions pass with zero flagged side-effects.
Impure side-effects during render (mutating external state) are detected.

specifications: React Official Docs: Keeping Components Pure
React Source: ReactStrictMode.js (Double-invoking component renders in dev)
verifiedRules: Render phase must be pure and free of observable side effects.
Side effects must be deferred strictly to the commit phase (useEffect / useLayoutEffect).
